title: CI Guardian Pull-Request Evaluation Result
description: Data contract for the CI Guardian's automated evaluation of an incoming Pull Request (issue #37). One evaluation covers exactly one PR head state. The Guardian derives its decision from a fixed criteria catalog that maps 1:1 onto the real public-boundary guards (.github/workflows/pipeline.yml) and the landing evaluation steps (.github/workflows/landing.yml), so a PASS verdict is always backed by machine-checked facts — never a hardcoded status (AGENT_RULES.md §13 bans fake health/pass status). Human-readable companion: docs/GUARDIAN_EVALUATION.md.

schema_version.description: Contract version of this evaluation result. The criteria catalog and decision rules are SSOT'd in docs/GUARDIAN_EVALUATION.md; any rule change MUST bump this version so downstream consumers (auto-merge workflows, private-side CI Guardian, audit tooling) can distinguish contract generations.

pr_number.description: The evaluated pull request number in the target repository.

head_sha.description: Full 40-hex git commit SHA of the evaluated PR head. Evaluations are immutable per head SHA: a new push always produces a new evaluation record, never an update to a previous one.

repository.description: Owner/name of the repository the PR targets (e.g. 'Supremeai-bd/supremeai-open'). Required when evaluations are cross-published to the federation; optional for single-repo guardians because the evaluation is normally bound to the repository that ran it.

guardian_id.description: Identifier of the guardian instance that produced this evaluation (e.g. 'merge-gate-public' for the public auto-landing workflow, 'ci-guardian-private' for the private monorepo's CI Guardian). Enables federation-wide audit of which surface made which decision.

evaluated_at.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC timestamp at which the evaluation completed (e.g. '2026-10-16T03:30:00Z').

decision.description: Guardian verdict. PASS = every criterion passed; the PR is eligible for autonomous landing (subject to the merge queue). HOLD = at least one healable criterion failed or was skipped — the finding is fixable in-channel (rebase, template fix, evidence), so the PR waits. REJECT = at least one integrity-class criterion (security_scan, scope_boundary, duplicate_free) failed — the PR must be reworked, it cannot be healed by a comment. Decision mapping is normative in docs/GUARDIAN_EVALUATION.md §2.

decision_reason.description: Human-readable sentence stating WHY the decision was reached, naming the failing criterion identifiers when the decision is not PASS. Posted verbatim in the guardian's PR comment (e.g. the 'Merge Gate — BLOCKED' landing comment).

criteria.description: Per-criterion evaluation records. Every criterion in the run's catalog MUST appear exactly once — a criterion that could not run is recorded with status 'skipped' and a reason, never omitted (omission would fake a pass by absence).

score.description: Informational aggregate: sum of weights of criteria with status 'pass'. Skipped and failed criteria contribute 0 (a skipped tier is never credited as a pass — AGENT_RULES.md §13). The score is a reporting aid only; eligibility is NOT score-based, it is the fail-closed conjunction defined by autonomous_merge_eligible.

autonomous_merge_eligible.description: The autonomous merge eligibility threshold (issue #37): true if and only if every criterion in the catalog has status 'pass'. This is a strict conjunction — there is no partial-credit path to landing, matching the real gate behavior (any failing or pending check holds the landing; .github/workflows/landing.yml watches all checks to terminal state and fails on any failure). MUST be true exactly when decision == 'PASS'.

healing_instructions.description: Aggregated, ordered remediation steps for the PR author, assembled from the failing criteria's healing_instructions. Required whenever decision is HOLD or REJECT; forbidden (absent or empty) on PASS because a passing PR has nothing to heal.

guard_results_url.description: Optional deep link to the workflow run or check suite backing this evaluation (e.g. the pipeline.yml run URL), for audit traceability from the verdict back to raw logs.

criterionId.description: Identifier of one evaluation criterion. The catalog is grounded in the public boundary: the first six guard jobs of .github/workflows/pipeline.yml (branch-naming-guard, issue-reference-guard, duplicate-pr-guard, boundary_sanitization_guard, loop_contract_parity_guard) plus the validation matrix, the secrets-scan job, and the landing.yml evaluation steps. AGENT_RULES.md §15 carries the federation-side GUARD-* IDs; the mapping table lives in docs/GUARDIAN_EVALUATION.md §3.

criterionStatus.description: Outcome of one criterion. 'skipped' is an honest third state: the check could not run (e.g. workflow infra failure). It never counts as a pass and it blocks autonomous merge eligibility.

weight.description: This criterion's contribution to the 0-100 score when passed. Weights across the catalog SHOULD sum to 100; weight 0 marks purely informational criteria that still block eligibility when not passed (blocking is status-driven, not weight-driven).

detail.description: Machine-derived factual finding for this criterion (e.g. 'head branch docs/foo matches ^(feat|fix|docs|chore|agent)/' or 'gitleaks: 0 secret families detected'). Must describe what was actually checked — fabricated or hardcoded statuses are forbidden (AGENT_RULES.md §13).

source.description: Where the fact came from: workflow job id, script, or API field (e.g. 'pipeline.yml/branch-naming-guard', 'landing.yml/evaluate', 'gh pr view .mergeable').

healing_instructions.description: Concrete remediation steps for this criterion when status is 'fail'. Required on fail so the author always receives actionable healing guidance (issue #37: 'Pass / Hold / Reject with automated healing instructions'). SHOULD be command-level where possible (e.g. 'git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main').

criterionResult.description: One criterion result. A 'fail' record MUST carry healing_instructions; 'pass' and 'skipped' records may omit them (a skipped criterion explains itself via detail + top-level healing instead).

allOf.description: Cross-field contract: PASS verdicts are all-green verdicts.
Cross-field contract: HOLD/REJECT verdicts always name the finding and always ship healing instructions.
Cross-field contract: REJECT is reserved for integrity-class failures — at least one of security_scan, scope_boundary, duplicate_free must have status 'fail'.
Cross-field contract: decision PASS requires every recorded criterion to have status 'pass' — no skipped, no failed (mirrors the real gate: any non-terminal or failing check holds the landing).
